title: The Orbit of Sector Nine
premise: Casper Montrose smuggles forbidden memories through the decaying orbital ring of Sector Nine, trading in the past of a colony Earth has written off. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with its crew mysteriously aged backward, Casper discovers her own mother among them—younger than Casper herself and carrying a memory core that holds the colony's true founding sin. Pursued by customs enforcers who want the core destroyed, Casper races to the dead relay at the edge of Sector Nine to broadcast the truth before Earth's final transmission loop closes forever. She succeeds at the cost of the relay—and of letting her mother's restored memories overwrite the woman she knew—choosing inheritance over love, and sending Sector Nine's story into the dark on its own terms.
about_author: Cyrus Montrose is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for decommissioned space stations before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they repair antique radios and insist that every signal deserves one last listener.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Heart
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs introduces Casper's trade in illegal memory-records and her quiet grief for a colony Earth has abandoned. She carries a client's dying father's last memories past inspection, feeling both courier and thief. Emotional beat: tender melancholy—the cost of carrying other people's pasts while refusing to face her own.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The Halcyon docks after forty years in deep space, its crew inexplicably aged backward into their twenties. Customs seals the ship; Casper is hired to extract one crewman's memories before enforcers wipe them. Inside his mind she glimpses a name that stops her cold: Veyra Montrose. Emotional beat: vertigo and dread as the impossible becomes personal.

chapters.title: Mother, Younger Than Me
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Casper breaches the Halcyon's sealed decks and finds her mother alive, de-aged, with no memory of raising her. Veyra clutches a black memory core she doesn't understand but refuses to surrender. Enforcers close in. Emotional beat: aching disorientation—grief and hope tangled, a reunion with someone who never knew you.

chapters.title: What the Core Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper and fragments from the core itself. Sampling the core in a safehouse, Casper learns Sector Nine was founded on a deliberate abandonment protocol: Earth chose the colony's slow death and erased the decision. Her mother helped record the evidence before fleeing deep space. Emotional beat: righteous fury hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Customs House Dogs
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Inspector Rhee—a customs officer with her own buried memories of Sector Nine—catches Casper but hesitates, offering an uneasy truce: deliver the core or watch it be destroyed. Meanwhile enforcers burn the safehouse network, killing Casper's fence and oldest friend. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve; trust extended across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: POV: Casper, with Veyra aboard. Casper steals a derelict tug and runs for the dead relay at the edge of Sector Nine, Veyra navigating on instincts older than her new body. In the quiet weeks between stations, mother and daughter circle each other—Veyra asks what kind of woman she became; Casper can't answer honestly. Emotional beat: fragile intimacy built on absence.

chapters.title: Signal Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. At a fuel depot, they intercept Earth's transmission loop: the countdown confirming the final broadcast window closes in nine days, after which no signal from Sector Nine will ever reach human ears again. Enforcer ships pick up their trail. Veyra confesses she volunteered for the de-aging experiment to carry the core home. Emotional beat: the clock starts; sacrifice reframed as love.

chapters.title: Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The relay looms, derelict and freezing. Enforcers ambush them in the approach; Rhee arrives unexpectedly and turns her guns on her own side, buying Casper minutes. Veyra takes a hull breach shielding the core. Dying young again, she gives Casper the core freely: 'You're the memory now.' Emotional beat: devastating climax of love against duty.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Alone in the relay's dead heart, Casper splices the core into the ancient transmitter as enforcers breach the hull. She must choose: broadcast the founding sin, or splice in her own recorded memories of her mother instead. She sends both—truth and love braided into one signal—as the loop closes around it. Emotional beat: transcendent defiance.

chapters.title: Orbit
chapters.summary: POV: Casper, epilogue voice. Months later, Sector Nine hums with renewed purpose as colonies across the fringe receive the broadcast and begin answering back. Casper keeps smuggling—but now she carries messages outward, not contraband inward. She visits her mother's grave in orbit and lets the last of her own recordings go. Emotional beat: quiet peace; inheritance accepted, memory set free.
